owner_notes: See PROGRAM.md for the words and PROGRESSION.md for what the progression rules mean. Loads are strings. Extra fields beyond the agreed shape: per_side (on an exercise, and on a block; the exercise wins), work_seconds, fixed, required, target_on_rung.

exercises.name: Indian club warmup
exercises.cue: Hold one light club in each hand and draw small, smooth circles in front of you and out to the side, two minutes each way. Keep the circles small and the shoulders down; big fast circles are the fault.

exercises.name: Mobility moves for the day
exercises.cue: Two minutes of the moves named for the day, slow and easy, moving through the full range without forcing. Do not stretch into pain; this is to warm up, not to gain range.

exercises.name: Yoga flow
exercises.cue: Move through the positions listed, three to five slow breaths in each, two rounds. Breathe out as you settle deeper. Do not bounce or push into a sharp stretch.

exercises.name: Couch stretch and calf stretch
exercises.cue: Couch stretch: kneel with the back foot up on a couch or chair, hips forward, 45 seconds each side. Calf stretch: hands on a wall, back leg straight, heel down, 45 seconds each side. Easy pressure, never a jolt.

exercises.name: Tibialis raise
exercises.cue: Stand with your back flat on a wall, feet about a foot out, and lift both sets of toes toward your shins as high as you can, then lower slowly. Keep the heels down and the knees straight; do not rock.

exercises.name: Slow calf raise, both legs
exercises.cue: Stand on the edge of a step with heels hanging off, rise up for three seconds, lower for three seconds to a full stretch at the bottom. The fault is bouncing out of the bottom.

exercises.name: Slow calf raise, one leg
exercises.cue: Same slow calf raise on one leg, a hand on the wall for balance only. Three seconds up, three down. Do not let the ankle roll outward at the top.

exercises.name: Slow calf raise, one leg, 18 lb
exercises.cue: The one-leg slow calf raise holding the 18 lb bell in the hand on the working side, other hand on the wall. Keep the three second tempo; speed is the fault.

exercises.name: Wall sit
exercises.cue: Back flat on a wall, slide down until the thighs are near level, knees over ankles, and hold still. Breathe. Do not let the knees drift inward or the back come off the wall.

exercises.name: Split squat
exercises.cue: Stand with one foot a long step ahead, hand on a wall, and lower straight down for three seconds until the back knee nears the floor, then stand. The front knee tracks over the toes; letting it cave inward is the fault.

exercises.name: Split squat, 18 lb at the chest
exercises.cue: The split squat holding the 18 lb bell at the chest with both hands. Same three second lower, same straight front knee.

exercises.name: Split squat, 36 lb at the chest
exercises.cue: The split squat holding the 36 lb bell at the chest. Keep the chest tall and the three second lower; do not shorten the stride to make it easier.

exercises.name: Goblet squat, 18 lb
exercises.cue: Hold the 18 lb bell against the chest by the horns, feet a little wider than hips, and sit deep between the knees, elbows inside the knees at the bottom, then stand. Heels stay down; rising onto the toes is the fault.

exercises.name: Goblet squat, 18 lb, 3 s down, 2 s pause
exercises.cue: The goblet squat with the 18 lb bell, three seconds down and a two second still pause at the bottom before standing. Stay tall in the pause; do not relax into it.

exercises.name: Goblet squat, 36 lb
exercises.cue: The goblet squat holding the 36 lb bell at the chest. Same deep sit, same flat heels. Do not let the bell pull you forward.

exercises.name: Goblet squat, 36 lb, 3 s down, 2 s pause
exercises.cue: The goblet squat with the 36 lb bell, three seconds down and a two second pause at the bottom. Breathe out on the way up.

exercises.name: Step-up, low step
exercises.cue: Step fully onto a low step with one foot, stand tall on it, then lower yourself back down over three seconds with that same leg. Do not push off the floor foot; the top leg does the work.

exercises.name: Step-up, low step, 18 lb
exercises.cue: The step-up holding the 18 lb bell at the chest with both hands. Same slow lower; do not drop.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.cue: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, and push the hips up until the body is a straight line from shoulders to knees, pause two seconds, lower. Squeeze the glutes at the top; arching the lower back is the fault.

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
exercises.cue: The glute bridge on one leg, the other knee pulled toward the chest. Hips stay level; one hip dropping is the fault.

exercises.name: Kettlebell row, 36 lb
exercises.cue: One hand on a chair seat, feet staggered, pull the 36 lb bell from a hang up to the hip, squeeze two seconds, lower slowly. The back stays flat and the shoulder stays down; shrugging is the fault.

exercises.name: Kettlebell row, 36 lb, 2 s pause at the top
exercises.cue: The 36 lb row with a two second still pause at the top of every rep. Do not twist the trunk to lift the bell higher.

exercises.name: Push-up, hands on a chair seat
exercises.cue: Hands on the seat of a sturdy chair, body straight from head to heels, lower the chest to the seat and press back up. Keep the hips in line; sagging or piking is the fault.

exercises.name: Push-up, knees down
exercises.cue: Push-up from the knees, hands under the shoulders, body straight from head to knees. Chest to the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees. Do not flare the elbows wide.

exercises.name: Push-up
exercises.cue: Full push-up, hands under the shoulders, body a straight plank, chest to the floor and back up. Hips move with the chest; a sagging middle is the fault.

exercises.name: Push-up, feet raised
exercises.cue: The full push-up with the feet on a low step so more weight is on the arms. Keep the body straight and the head neutral.

exercises.name: Push-up, band across the back
exercises.cue: The full push-up with a band across the upper back, ends under the hands, so the top of the rep is heavier. Do not let the band pull the shoulders forward at the bottom.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press, 18 lb
exercises.cue: Stand tall holding the 18 lb bell at the shoulder, press it straight overhead until the arm locks, lower it slowly. Ribs stay down; leaning back to finish the press is the fault.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press, 18 lb, 5 s lower
exercises.cue: The 18 lb press with a five second lower on every rep. Press at normal speed, lower slow. Do not let the elbow drift out to the side.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press, 18 lb, bottoms up
exercises.cue: Hold the 18 lb bell upside down by the handle, bell above the fist, and press it overhead while keeping it balanced. Crush the handle. If it tips, stop the set.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press, 36 lb, half kneeling
exercises.cue: Kneel on one knee, the other foot forward, and press the 36 lb bell overhead from the shoulder on the side of the down knee. The kneeling position stops you leaning; keep the ribs down.

exercises.name: Kettlebell press, 36 lb
exercises.cue: Standing press with the 36 lb bell, straight up, slow down. Brace the trunk before each press; do not bend back.

exercises.name: Band pull-apart
exercises.cue: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight, and pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest, then return slowly. Shoulders stay down; shrugging up is the fault.

exercises.name: Bow trainer draw, 3 s hold at full draw
exercises.cue: Draw the bow trainer as you would a bow, elbow high and back, hold three seconds at full draw, release slowly. The pulling shoulder blade moves toward the spine; do not let the front shoulder hunch.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.cue: Forearms and toes on the floor, body a straight line, glutes tight, breathe steadily. Hips sagging or rising is the fault; stop the hold when the line goes.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry, 36 lb
exercises.cue: Pick up the 36 lb bell in one hand like a suitcase and walk tall for the time, then switch hands. Do not lean away from the bell; the trunk stays square.

exercises.name: Grip hold, towel through the 36 lb handle
exercises.cue: Loop a towel through the handle of the 36 lb bell, grip the towel in one hand and let the bell hang at your side for the time. Shoulders back and down; do not let the shoulder round forward.

exercises.name: Dead hang
exercises.cue: Grip the bar with both hands and hang with straight arms, shoulders pulled slightly down away from the ears, feet off the floor. Do not let the shoulders rise into the ears.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing intervals, 18 lb, 15 s on 45 s off
exercises.cue: Swing the 18 lb bell between the legs and up to chest height by snapping the hips forward, for 15 seconds, then rest 45 seconds. Hinge at the hips with a flat back; squatting the swing is the fault. You should be able to speak a full sentence.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing intervals, 18 lb, 20 s on 40 s off
exercises.cue: The kettlebell swing for 20 seconds on, 40 off. Same hip snap, same flat back. Stop early if the form goes.

exercises.name: Kettlebell swing intervals, 18 lb, 20 s on 20 s off
exercises.cue: The kettlebell swing for 20 seconds on, 20 off. Harder phase; a few words of speech, not a sentence. Flat back, hips do the work.

exercises.name: Step-up intervals, 40 s on 20 s off
exercises.cue: Step up and down on a low step at a steady walking rhythm for 40 seconds, rest 20, changing the lead leg each round. Place the whole foot on the step; do not go fast enough to lose control.

exercises.name: Mace 360 intervals, 30 s on 30 s off
exercises.cue: Hold the mace with both hands at the bottom of the handle and swing the head in a circle behind you from one shoulder to the other, 30 seconds on, 30 off. Keep the trunk still and the elbows soft; letting the head pull your shoulders back is the fault.

exercises.name: Mace 10-to-2
exercises.cue: From the mace held in front, swing the head behind you and back to the front on the same side, as on a clock from 10 to 2, then the other side. Slow and controlled. Do not let the lower back arch to catch the weight.

exercises.name: Jump rope intervals, 20 s on 40 s off
exercises.cue: Jump rope with both feet together, a low bounce, soft knees, 20 seconds on, 40 off. Land quietly on the balls of the feet; a high jump or landing flat-footed is the fault.

exercises.name: Jump rope intervals, 30 s on 30 s off
exercises.cue: Jump rope with both feet, 30 seconds on, 30 off. Same low quiet bounce. Stop a round early if the calves or shins start to hurt rather than burn.

exercises.name: Brisk walk
exercises.cue: Walk fast enough to breathe harder but still talk, for the time. This brings the heart down after the intervals; do not sit straight down.

exercises.name: Walk
exercises.cue: An easy walk at a pace where talking is comfortable. Log the distance. Nothing to get right.

exercises.name: Ruck, 10 lb pack
exercises.cue: Walk with 10 lb in a backpack, straps snug so the pack does not swing, at a pace where you can talk easily. Log the distance and the minutes. Do not lean forward to carry the weight.

exercises.name: Ruck, 15 lb pack
exercises.cue: Walk with 15 lb in a backpack, same easy talking pace, pack snug. Log distance and minutes.

exercises.name: Ruck, 20 lb pack
exercises.cue: Walk with 20 lb in a backpack, same easy pace. Stand tall under the pack; log distance and minutes.

workouts.name: Easy ruck or walk
workouts.focus: low effort heart hours, Mudder miles

blocks.notes: A pace where you can talk easily. 30 to 60 minutes. Distance first, then weight, never both in one week. No pack: log a walk instead.
Optional. Easy. Rest days are rest.

second.message: Two pain marks on this exercise in a month. See a physio or doctor before it comes back. Unpark it yourself when they say so.

requires.prompt: Have you asked your doctor whether there is any limit on how hard you push intervals? Yes means you asked, whatever the answer.
requires.if_limit_set: keep closed and flag trainer review

params.note: A light workout finished in place of a required one changes no streaks. Rest days with nothing logged are not misses.
